newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian call ends at 3.03.25 pct, gilt prices fall.
newsitem.headline: Indian call ends at 3.03.25 pct, gilt prices fall.

text.p: Indian call money ended Wednesday at 3.0-3.25 percent after trading in a tight range for most of the day, dealers said.
They said most of the day's trade was between 2.75 percent and 3.0 percent, with stray deals at 3.50 percent.
Dealers said liquidity with banks remained good but rates could open slightly higher on Thursday due to funds outflows towards a repos auction.
The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) holds a four-day repos auction of government of India securities later on Wednesday and payments by successful bidders are to be made on Thursday.
"The outflow towards the auction will have some impact on call money tomorrow," said a dealer at a state-run bank. "But rates should be stable in a 5.0-5.5 percent range."
Dealers said prices of government securities fell in thin trade on Wednesday. Prices fell on profit-taking by market participants, they said.
Dealers said trade was light as market participants stayed on the sidelines ahead of the repos auction.
"Market players are waiting to see how much funds go out at the auction," said a dealer. "The post-auction liquidity will determine their investment decisions."

The 12 percent 1999 government of India stock traded on Wednesday at 100.08 rupees against its last traded 100.18, the 13.50 percent 1997 at 101.67 against 101.72 and the 13.50 percent 1998 fell to 103.27 from 103.30, dealers said.

Yields on treasury bills ended mixed, they said. March maturity treasury bills yielded 5.0 percent against last yield of 5.5 percent, April bills 7.7 percent against 7.65 and July bills 9.25 percent against 9.15 percent.
Dealers said there were no trades in commercial paper or certificates of deposit.
